advances: In the actual canonical positive-fresh hard branch, almost-total optimizer load and the complete recomputed product reservoir force a macroscopic, edge-capacity-disjoint family of genuine physical-midpoint collisions. More precisely, one can pair distinct loaded reservoir edges having the same physical midpoint, with no edge used beyond the actual submatching \(s\), and obtain total label mass greater than \(373Q/19200\). Every label is a centrally symmetric four-source configuration contained in one occupied affine slice of rank at most two. If every occupied-rank-at-most-two slice score is less than \(\varepsilon S\), this mass must be distributed over more than \((373/(19200\varepsilon))2^n\) distinct affine slices. The paired contact and centroid averages also admit explicit one-body, one-use Jensen packings at every physical midpoint. Thus the remaining positive-fresh bridge is no longer the existence of collision mass or a no-reuse Jensen ledger: it is a fusion theorem for a super-dyadic family of rank-at-most-two collision slices whose two pooled continuous fields both retain high residual rank.

proof:
We first record the two global scalar estimates that force collisions. In one good parity class \(\xi\), direct summation of (2) gives
\[
 \sum_{\substack{u<v\\u,v\equiv\xi}}r_{\{u,v\}}
 =\frac{A_\xi^2-\sum_{z\equiv\xi}a_z^2}{8A_\xi}
 \leq\frac{A_\xi}{8}.
\tag{41}
\]
Summing over good classes gives \(Q\leq W/8\). Thus (6) gives \(G<W/2\), so accepted fact c81f02314cb34f8b applies to the present actual reservoir and yields
\[
 Q\geq\frac3{32}(W-4G).
\tag{42}
\]
Rearranging (42) and using (6),
\[
 W\leq\frac{32}{3}Q+4G
 <\left(\frac{32}{3}+\frac1{25}\right)Q
 =\frac{803}{75}Q.
\tag{43}
\]

If \(e\notin\mathcal H\), then \(r_e-\omega_e>r_e/2\). Therefore (4) gives
\[
 \sum_{e\notin\mathcal H}r_e
 <2\sum_e(r_e-\omega_e)
 =2(Q-\Omega)
 <\frac Q{50}.
\tag{44}
\]
Subtracting (44) from \(Q\) proves (13).

Fix a reservoir edge \(e=\{u,v\}\) in the good class \(\xi\), and put \(m=m_e\). Accepted fact 32aedd8da549416a gives
\[
 a_m\geq\beta_e
 =\left(\frac{a_u^{1/d}+a_v^{1/d}}2\right)^d
 \geq\sqrt{a_ua_v}.
\tag{45}
\]
Goodness gives \(a_u,a_v\leq A_\xi/4\), and hence
\[
 \sqrt{a_ua_v}\leq\frac{A_\xi}{4}.
\tag{46}
\]
Using (2), equations (45)-(46) give
\[
 16r_e
 =\frac{4a_ua_v}{A_\xi}
 =4\sqrt{a_ua_v}
   \frac{\sqrt{a_ua_v}}{A_\xi}
 \leq\sqrt{a_ua_v}
 \leq a_m.
\tag{47}
\]
For every physical target with \(\mathcal H_m\ne\varnothing\), choose an edge attaining \(r_m^{\max}\). Equation (47), summed over the distinct physical target fibers, and then (43), give
\[
 16\sum_mr_m^{\max}
 \leq\sum_ma_m
 \leq W
 <\frac{803}{75}Q.
\tag{48}
\]
This proves (14). Subtracting (14) from (13), target by target, proves (15).

We construct the no-reuse collision pairing. Fix a target \(m\) and assign to every edge \(e\in\mathcal H_m\) the occurrence capacity
\[
 c_e:=\frac{r_e}{8},
 \qquad
 C_m^{\mathcal H}:=\sum_{e\in\mathcal H_m}c_e,
 \qquad
 c_m^{\max}:=\max_{e\in\mathcal H_m}c_e.
\tag{49}
\]
The exact off-diagonal fractional degree criterion used in accepted fact c81f02314cb34f8b gives a pairing of these edge occurrences of mass
\[
 P_m=
 \min\left\{
 \frac{C_m^{\mathcal H}}2,
 C_m^{\mathcal H}-c_m^{\max}
 \right\}.
\tag{50}
\]
For completeness, if \(2c_m^{\max}\leq C_m^{\mathcal H}\), all capacities are the degrees of an off-diagonal fractional matching and the mass is \(C_m^{\mathcal H}/2\). If \(2c_m^{\max}>C_m^{\mathcal H}\), match every nonmaximal occurrence directly to a maximal one; this has mass \(C_m^{\mathcal H}-c_m^{\max}\) and respects the maximal capacity. Thus no loop is used in either case. Equation (50) always gives
\[
 P_m\geq
 \frac{C_m^{\mathcal H}-c_m^{\max}}2
 =\frac{R_m^{\mathcal H}-r_m^{\max}}{16}.
\tag{51}
\]
Choose such a pairing independently at every target and denote its edge-pair weights by \(\lambda_{\{e,f\}}\). Its degree at edge \(e\) is at most \(c_e=r_e/8\). If \(e\in\mathcal H\), equations (5) and (10) give
\[
 s_e\geq\frac{\omega_e}{4}
 \geq\frac{r_e}{8}=c_e,
\tag{52}
\]
which proves (17). Summing (51) and using (15) gives
\[
 \Pi>\frac1{16}\frac{373Q}{1200}
 =\frac{373Q}{19200}.
\tag{53}
\]
Since \(s_e\leq r_e\) for every edge, \(S\leq Q\), and (19) follows.

Let \(L=\{e,f\}\) be a positive pairing label as in (20). If the two distinct unordered edges shared an endpoint, equality of their midpoints would force their other endpoints to agree, making the two edges equal. Hence their four endpoints are distinct. Write
\[
 u=m+a,
 \quad v=m-a,
 \quad u'=m+b,
 \quad v'=m-b.
\tag{54}
\]
All four points lie in \(m+\operatorname{span}\{a,b\}\), and they span exactly the affine space in (21). Thus its dimension is at most two. Equation (22) is the direct fiberwise consequence of convexity of \(C\).

Fix an affine subspace \(A\). Each label counted by \(\Lambda(A)\) contributes \(\lambda_L\) to two distinct edges and hence contributes four endpoint incidences, all based in \(A\). Summing first over labels, then over their edge occurrences and endpoints, and finally using (17), gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 4\Lambda(A)
 &\leq
 \sum_{z\in I_+\cap A}
 \sum_{e\ni z}d_e(\lambda)\\
 &\leq
 \sum_{z\in I_+\cap A}
 \sum_{e\ni z}s_e
 =b_A(s).
 \end{aligned}
\tag{55}
\]
This proves (25). For a minimal label hull \(A_L\), the four endpoints belong to \(I_+\cap A_L\) and span \(A_L\), so the occupied rank \(q_{A_L}\) equals \(q_L\leq2\). Equations (25) and (27) give, for every exact-hull group,
\[
 \sum_{L:A_L=A}\lambda_L
 \leq\Lambda(A)
 <\frac{\varepsilon S}{4\,2^{n-q_A}}
 \leq\varepsilon 2^{-n}S,
\tag{56}
\]
because \(q_A\leq2\). Dividing the total lower bound (19) by the per-group upper bound (56) proves (29).

Every pairing label contributes its weight once to each of its two edge
occurrences, so summing degrees in (17) gives
\[
 |w|=\sum_ed_e(\lambda)=2\sum_L\lambda_L=2\Pi.
\tag{56a}
\]
Equations (17), (19), and \(S\leq Q\) prove (29b). Applying the first
screen in (29c) to this particular nonzero field \(w\), and then using
(29b), gives
\[
 r_w^\ell+1>
 2^{n-\rho_w}\frac{|w|}{\varepsilon S}
 >\frac{373}{9600\varepsilon}2^{n-\rho_w}.
\tag{56b}
\]
The centroid screen gives the second inequality in (29d) identically.

It remains to prove the two Jensen packings. Equation (45) and (47) imply
\[
 \beta_e\geq16r_e,
 \qquad
 \vartheta_e=\frac{\beta_e}{2}\geq8r_e.
\tag{57}
\]
For every source parity color \(\xi\) and physical target \(m\), the exact product-root estimate in accepted fact fc18c3c4832f0bfb, under the canonical aliases retained in da867120a5f52797, gives
\[
 \sum_{\substack{e\in\mathcal H_m\\e\subseteq\xi}}
 \frac{r_e}{\vartheta_e}\leq\frac14.
\tag{58}
\]
Since \(\beta_e=2\vartheta_e\), it also gives
\[
 \sum_{\substack{e\in\mathcal H_m\\e\subseteq\xi}}
 \frac{r_e}{\beta_e}\leq\frac18.
\tag{59}
\]

For a positive label \(L=\{e,f\}\) at target \(m\), define the contact component density
\[
 F_L^\ell
 :=\frac{\lambda_L}{2\vartheta_e}\varphi_e
  +\frac{\lambda_L}{2\vartheta_f}\varphi_f
 \quad\text{on }C_m.
\tag{60}
\]
It has mass \(\lambda_L\) and barycenter
\((\ell_e+\ell_f)/2\). At one physical target, sum (60) over all positive labels. Using the pairing degrees, (17), and then (58) over at most \(2^n\) colors,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{L:m_L=m}F_L^\ell
 &\leq\frac12
 \sum_{e\in\mathcal H_m}
 \frac{d_e(\lambda)}{\vartheta_e}\\
 &\leq\frac1{16}
 \sum_{e\in\mathcal H_m}
 \frac{r_e}{\vartheta_e}
 \leq\frac1{16}\,2^n\frac14
 =2^{n-6}.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{61}
\]
Here the first inequality is pointwise and also uses \(0\leq\varphi_e\leq1\). Therefore
\[
 F_m^\ell:=
 \alpha_\ell\sum_{L:m_L=m}F_L^\ell
\tag{62}
\]
satisfies \(0\leq F_m^\ell\leq1\), has mass \(\alpha_\ell\Pi_m\), and has normalized first moment \(y_m^\ell\). This proves the first membership in (35).

Accepted fact 32aedd8da549416a gives
\(\bar c_e\in\mathsf M_{\beta_e}(C_{m_e})\), so witnesses (31) exist. Define
\[
 F_L^c
 :=\frac{\lambda_L}{2\beta_e}\psi_e
  +\frac{\lambda_L}{2\beta_f}\psi_f.
\tag{63}
\]
It has mass \(\lambda_L\) and barycenter
\((\bar c_e+\bar c_f)/2\). Equations (17) and (59) give the sharper pointwise bound
\[
 \sum_{L:m_L=m}F_L^c
 \leq\frac1{16}
 \sum_{e\in\mathcal H_m}\frac{r_e}{\beta_e}
 \leq\frac1{16}\,2^n\frac18
 =2^{n-7}.
\tag{64}
\]
Thus
\[
 F_m^c:=\alpha_c\sum_{L:m_L=m}F_L^c
\tag{65}
\]
is one legal density on \(C_m\), of mass \(\alpha_c\Pi_m\) and barycenter \(y_m^c\). This proves the second membership in (35). The construction first aggregates every component belonging to one physical target and only then invokes a metronoid, so target collisions and repeated continuous atoms do not reuse a fiber.

Accepted fact 6769574fc1bd9f8d applied to (35) gives
\[
 \delta_C(m,y_m^\ell)\geq
 \gamma_d\alpha_\ell\Pi_m,
 \qquad
 \delta_C(m,y_m^c)\geq
 \gamma_d\alpha_c\Pi_m.
\tag{66}
\]
For a closed ambient halfspace, sum (66) over exactly the atoms it contains. Distinct atoms in either measure (39) have distinct physical base fibers, so the corresponding fiber sections of \(C\) are disjoint terms of the mixed-volume measure. This proves halfspace domination for both measures. Applying the dominated-measure residual theorem of accepted fact be359f8a6c628483 and multiplying its depth bound by \(2^n\) proves (40).

All uses of a reservoir edge in (16), (55), (60), and (63) are bounded by its single pairing degree, which is at most \(r_e/8\leq s_e\). All uses of a physical target in (62) and (65) are aggregated before the depth theorem. Thus the construction is weighted and no-reuse at both interfaces. Equations (28)-(29) show why it does not yet close the positive-fresh hard branch: after every individual rank-at-most-two slice is subterminal, the macroscopic label mass may still be dispersed among a super-dyadic number of distinct slices, and (40) still permits both pooled residual ranks to be large. This completes the proof.
statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, and retain the exact common canonical positive-fresh hard objects, normalizations, contacts, and aliases of accepted fact da867120a5f52797. Thus
\[
 C_z:=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:(z,x)\in C\},
 \qquad
 a_z:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z),
 \qquad
 I_+:=\{z\in\mathbb Z^n:a_z>0\},
 \qquad
 W:=\sum_{z\in I_+}a_z,
\tag{1}
\]
\(r=(r_e)\) is the half-strength canonical product reservoir, and, on a good parity class \(\xi\),
\[
 A_\xi:=\sum_{z\equiv\xi\pmod2}a_z,
 \qquad
 r_{\{u,v\}}=\frac{a_ua_v}{4A_\xi}
 \quad
 (u\ne v,\ u\equiv v\equiv\xi\pmod2).
\tag{2}
\]
Put
\[
 Q:=\sum_er_e>0.
\tag{3}
\]
The original load-minimal optimizer and the single-optimizer submatching are
\[
 0\leq\omega_e\leq r_e,
 \qquad
 \Omega:=\sum_e\omega_e>\frac{99Q}{100},
\tag{4}
\]
\[
 s_e=\left(1-\frac34\chi_{m_e}\right)\omega_e,
 \qquad
 \frac{\omega_e}{4}\leq s_e\leq\omega_e\leq r_e,
 \qquad
 S:=\sum_es_e>\frac{99Q}{400},
\tag{5}
\]
where \(m_e=(u+v)/2\) for \(e=\{u,v\}\). The hard ledger includes
\(G:=\mathfrak C_{\mathrm{core}}(C)\) and
\[
 G<\frac Q{100}.
\tag{6}
\]
For every positive-load edge, retain its exposed contact \(\ell_e\), its endpoint decomposition, and its target root mass
\[
 \vartheta_e:=2^{-(d+1)}
 \bigl(a_u^{1/d}+a_v^{1/d}\bigr)^d,
 \qquad
 \ell_e\in\mathsf M_{\vartheta_e}(C_{m_e}).
\tag{7}
\]
For every \(z\in I_+\), put
\[
 c_z:=\frac1{a_z}\int_{C_z}x\,dx,
\tag{8}
\]
and, for \(e=\{u,v\}\), put
\[
 \bar c_e:=\frac{c_u+c_v}{2},
 \qquad
 \beta_e:=
 \left(\frac{a_u^{1/d}+a_v^{1/d}}2\right)^d
 =2\vartheta_e.
\tag{9}
\]

Define the heavy loaded edge set
\[
 \mathcal H:=\left\{e:\omega_e\geq\frac{r_e}{2}\right\}.
\tag{10}
\]
For every physical midpoint \(m\), put
\[
 \mathcal H_m:=\{e\in\mathcal H:m_e=m\},
 \qquad
 R_m^{\mathcal H}:=\sum_{e\in\mathcal H_m}r_e,
\tag{11}
\]
and, when \(\mathcal H_m\ne\varnothing\), put
\[
 r_m^{\max}:=\max_{e\in\mathcal H_m}r_e.
\tag{12}
\]
Then
\[
 \boxed{\sum_{e\in\mathcal H}r_e>\frac{49Q}{50},}
\tag{13}
\]
\[
 \boxed{\sum_{m:\mathcal H_m\ne\varnothing}r_m^{\max}
 <\frac{803Q}{1200},}
\tag{14}
\]
and hence the exact collision excess satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{m:\mathcal H_m\ne\varnothing}
 \bigl(R_m^{\mathcal H}-r_m^{\max}\bigr)
 >\frac{373Q}{1200}.}
\tag{15}
\]

There are nonnegative numbers
\[
 \lambda_{\{e,f\}}=\lambda_{\{f,e\}}
 \qquad
 (e\ne f,\ e,f\in\mathcal H,\ m_e=m_f),
\tag{16}
\]
with all other \(\lambda_{\{e,f\}}\) equal to zero, such that
\[
 d_e(\lambda):=
 \sum_{\substack{f\in\mathcal H_{m_e}\\f\ne e}}
 \lambda_{\{e,f\}}
 \leq\frac{r_e}{8}
 \leq s_e
 \qquad(e\in\mathcal H),
\tag{17}
\]
and, writing
\[
 \Pi_m:=
 \sum_{\{e,f\}\subseteq\mathcal H_m}
 \lambda_{\{e,f\}},
 \qquad
 \Pi:=\sum_m\Pi_m,
\tag{18}
\]
one has
\[
 \boxed{
 \Pi>\frac{373Q}{19200}
 \geq\frac{373S}{19200}.}
\tag{19}
\]
Thus \(\lambda\) is an edge-no-reuse submatching of the actual \(s\)-ledger, not merely of the reservoir.

Every positive label \(L=\{e,f\}\), where
\[
 e=\{u,v\},
 \qquad
 f=\{u',v'\},
 \qquad
 m_L:=m_e=m_f=m,
 \qquad
 \lambda_L:=\lambda_{\{e,f\}}>0,
\tag{20}
\]
has four distinct endpoints and lies in the affine subspace
\[
 A_L:=\operatorname{aff}\{u,v,u',v'\}
 =m+\operatorname{span}\{u-m,u'-m\},
 \qquad
 q_L:=\dim A_L\leq2.
\tag{21}
\]
Both actual convexity inclusions
\[
 \frac12(C_u+C_v)\subseteq C_m,
 \qquad
 \frac12(C_{u'}+C_{v'})\subseteq C_m
\tag{22}
\]
hold inside the same physical target fiber.

For an affine subspace \(A\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), put
\[
 b_A(s):=\sum_{z\in I_+\cap A}d_z(s),
 \qquad
 d_z(s):=\sum_{e\ni z}s_e,
\tag{23}
\]
and put
\[
 \Lambda(A):=
 \sum_{\substack{L=\{e,f\}:\lambda_L>0\\
                   \text{all four endpoints of }L\text{ lie in }A}}
 \lambda_L.
\tag{24}
\]
Then every affine subspace satisfies the no-reuse incidence inequality
\[
 \boxed{4\Lambda(A)\leq b_A(s).}
\tag{25}
\]
In particular, suppose that, for some \(\varepsilon>0\), every affine subspace \(A\) with
\[
 I_+\cap A\ne\varnothing,
 \qquad
 q_A:=\dim\operatorname{aff}(I_+\cap A)\leq2
\tag{26}
\]
satisfies the strict occupied-slice screen
\[
 2^{n-q_A}b_A(s)<\varepsilon S.
\tag{27}
\]
Group the positive labels by their exact minimal affine hull \(A_L\). For every such group,
\[
 \boxed{
 \sum_{L:A_L=A}\lambda_L
 <\varepsilon 2^{-n}S,}
\tag{28}
\]
and consequently the number \(N_{\mathrm{pl}}\) of distinct affine subspaces \(A_L\) carrying positive label mass obeys
\[
 \boxed{
 N_{\mathrm{pl}}>
 \frac{373}{19200\,\varepsilon}\,2^n.}
\tag{29}
\]

Define the paired edge-occurrence field
\[
 w_e:=d_e(\lambda)
 \qquad(e\in\mathcal H),
\tag{29a}
\]
and extend it by zero to the other reservoir edges. Then
\[
 \boxed{0\leq w\leq s,
 \qquad
 |w|:=\sum_ew_e=2\Pi>
 \frac{373Q}{9600}\geq\frac{373S}{9600}.}
\tag{29b}
\]
Let \(\rho_w\) be the affine rank of
\(\{m_e:w_e>0\}\), and let \(r_w^\ell,r_w^c\) be the intrinsic
continuous residual ranks of the fields
\((m_e,\ell_e)\) and \((m_e,\bar c_e)\), respectively, on this
positive support. For every nonzero edge field \(q\leq s\), define
\(|q|:=\sum_eq_e\), define \(\rho_q\) in the same way from
\(\{m_e:q_e>0\}\), and define
\(r_q^\ell,r_q^c\) as the corresponding intrinsic residual ranks of
the contact and centroid fields on that support. If, in addition to
(27), the two submatching screens
\[
 \sup_{0<q\leq s}
 2^{n-\rho_q}\frac{|q|}{r_q^\ell+1}<\varepsilon S,
 \qquad
 \sup_{0<q\leq s}
 2^{n-\rho_q}\frac{|q|}{r_q^c+1}<\varepsilon S
\tag{29c}
\]
hold, then this one macroscopic no-reuse collision field satisfies
\[
 \boxed{
 r_w^\ell+1>
 \frac{373}{9600\varepsilon}2^{n-\rho_w},
 \qquad
 r_w^c+1>
 \frac{373}{9600\varepsilon}2^{n-\rho_w}.}
\tag{29d}
\]

The collision pairing also has two exact one-body Jensen completions. For every heavy edge choose a density \(\varphi_e\) on \(C_{m_e}\) representing (7):
\[
 0\leq\varphi_e\leq1,
 \qquad
 \int_{C_{m_e}}\varphi_e=\vartheta_e,
 \qquad
 \int_{C_{m_e}}x\varphi_e(x)\,dx
 =\vartheta_e\ell_e.
\tag{30}
\]
Also choose a density \(\psi_e\) representing the accepted membership
\(\bar c_e\in\mathsf M_{\beta_e}(C_{m_e})\):
\[
 0\leq\psi_e\leq1,
 \qquad
 \int_{C_{m_e}}\psi_e=\beta_e,
 \qquad
 \int_{C_{m_e}}x\psi_e(x)\,dx
 =\beta_e\bar c_e.
\tag{31}
\]
Put
\[
 \alpha_\ell:=\min\{1,2^{6-n}\},
 \qquad
 \alpha_c:=\min\{1,2^{7-n}\}.
\tag{32}
\]
For every \(m\) with \(\Pi_m>0\), define
\[
 y_m^\ell:=\frac1{\Pi_m}
 \sum_{\{e,f\}\subseteq\mathcal H_m}
 \lambda_{\{e,f\}}\frac{\ell_e+\ell_f}{2},
\tag{33}
\]
\[
 y_m^c:=\frac1{\Pi_m}
 \sum_{\{e,f\}\subseteq\mathcal H_m}
 \lambda_{\{e,f\}}\frac{\bar c_e+\bar c_f}{2}.
\tag{34}
\]
Then the sums of the explicitly scaled component densities satisfy one physical-fiber budget and give
\[
 \boxed{
 y_m^\ell\in\mathsf M_{\alpha_\ell\Pi_m}(C_m),
 \qquad
 y_m^c\in\mathsf M_{\alpha_c\Pi_m}(C_m).}
\tag{35}
\]
No physical target fiber is used more than once in either membership.

Let
\[
 E_\Pi:=\{m:\Pi_m>0\},
 \qquad
 \rho_\ell=\rho_c:=\dim\operatorname{aff}(E_\Pi),
\tag{36}
\]
and define
\[
 r_\ell:=
 \min_{a:\operatorname{aff}(E_\Pi)\to\mathbb R^d\ {\rm affine}}
 \dim\operatorname{span}\{y_m^\ell-a(m):m\in E_\Pi\},
\tag{37}
\]
\[
 r_c:=
 \min_{a:\operatorname{aff}(E_\Pi)\to\mathbb R^d\ {\rm affine}}
 \dim\operatorname{span}\{y_m^c-a(m):m\in E_\Pi\}.
\tag{38}
\]
With \(\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d\), both measures
\[
 \nu_\ell:=
 \gamma_d\alpha_\ell
 \sum_{m\in E_\Pi}\Pi_m\delta_{(m,y_m^\ell)},
 \qquad
 \nu_c:=
 \gamma_d\alpha_c
 \sum_{m\in E_\Pi}\Pi_m\delta_{(m,y_m^c)}
\tag{39}
\]
are carried by \(C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\) and are separately halfspace-dominated by the mixed-volume measure of \(C\). Consequently, for \(D:=2^nh_{\max}(C)\),
\[
 \boxed{
 D\geq
 \gamma_d\alpha_\ell 2^{n-\rho_\ell}
 \frac{\Pi}{r_\ell+1},
 \qquad
 D\geq
 \gamma_d\alpha_c 2^{n-\rho_c}
 \frac{\Pi}{r_c+1}.}
\tag{40}
\]

Equations (13)-(40) do not by themselves prove a rank-free lower bound \(G+D\geq c_J S\). Under simultaneous failure of (40) and the slice screen (27), the exact remaining configuration is a macroscopic no-reuse family spread over more than a constant multiple of \(2^n/\varepsilon\) distinct occupied rank-at-most-two collision slices, while both physically pooled Jensen fields have high residual rank. A further fusion theorem across these distinct slices is required.
